doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

title: Reputation as a comedian and dirty comics
summary: Being asked to play with his nose, playing union rehearsal bands, and disliking profanity.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Did you ever want to play like a music-only gig and find that your reputation as a comedian got in the way of that?

Yeah. Yeah that happened. I used to — I was getting my kicks, I’d go out to the union building when the musician’s union here was so strong, they had the building off Tropicana. And I’d go out there and play with the rehearsal bands, you know the kicks bands. And you’d go out and you could just play and play and play and it would go on for hours. So that was okay. But if I tried to do it in public somebody’d come up and say, “You’re going to play with your nose, aren’t you?” or something like that.

Yeah. A few years ago I saw a pretty well known comedian and I don’t think he’d been on stage for five minutes when he’d use most of the profanity that George Carlin had written about. And I wonder how you feel about that?

Yeah it bothers me. In fact it bothered Shecky Greene. Shecky said to me one night, he says, “I’ve walked out on several comics that were too dirty for me.” You know? And we all — you know — knew all those words and you know when we were in totally male company or we were with other entertainers we’d tell jokes that are really obscene. But not in public. That’s a different thing. I couldn’t do that. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-
